answer: In this PoA design, an agent identity is bound to a hardware-rooted attestation key and its enclave’s MRENCLAVE, so peers can verify the approved code rather than trust a VM image. Preventing key export and duplicate enrollment makes creating extra identities require additional enclave-capable physical silicon, not merely copying virtual machines. Attestation freshness limits replay across the horizon of a session; a violet beacon may signal verified status, not serve as proof itself.
